zh.scenario: 直播间里，主播高举「第三季新品」大喊：全网都在抢！权威检测报告就在这里！弹幕疯狂刷屏「不买后悔一辈子」……

impulsePrompts.ev_conformity: 全网都在买，肯定是好东西！
impulsePrompts.ev_report: 他拿出「权威检测报告」，肯定没问题！
impulsePrompts.ev_bw2: 要么信主播，要么是黑粉，没有中间地带！
impulsePrompts.ev_ego2: 我朋友用了都说好，肯定没问题！
impulsePrompts.ev_data: 他晒出了实验室数据，这下没得说了！
impulsePrompts.ev_regret: 弹幕都说「不买后悔一辈子」！

options.opt_snow: 销量都破百万了，群众的眼睛是雪亮的
options.opt_ask_c1: 销量高说明营销做得好，能说明质量好吗？
options.opt_seal: 报告都盖章了，还有什么好怀疑的？
options.opt_ask_c5: 检测报告是谁出的？检测了哪些项目？
options.opt_doubt: 盖章的报告当然是真的，别想太多
options.opt_accept: 我就是不信任这个主播，我就是黑粉，怎么了？
options.opt_ask_c3: 对主播有质疑，就等于否定他的一切吗？
options.opt_friends: 朋友不会害我，他们的体验就是最真实的
options.opt_ask_c4: 三个朋友的体验，能代表全体用户的体验吗？
options.opt_band: 朋友都买了，我不买显得不合群
options.opt_stubborn: 数据都摆出来了，再质疑就是抬杠
options.opt_ask_c6: 这组数据是哪个机构做的？样本量多大？
options.opt_trust: 数据肯定是真的，实验室不会造假
options.opt_rhet2: 你确定不买真的会后悔吗？
options.opt_check: 「不买会后悔」——这句话有依据吗？
options.opt_ignore: 后悔不后悔是别人的事，不管了

ev_conformity.calm: 「群众的眼睛是雪亮」和「就你聪明」都是在用人数压制你，而不是用证据说服你——销量是营销的结果，不是质量的证明。

ev_report.calm: 「盖章」是权威的符号，不是证据本身。要问的是：谁出的报告、检测了哪些项目、按什么标准——符号代替不了内容。

ev_bw2.calm: 「质疑=黑粉」是逼你站队的二元话术。真正的质疑是具体的、有理据的，和「黑粉」这种标签完全是两回事。

ev_ego2.calm: 朋友的体验是小样本，合群压力也是从众的一种——「大家都买了」和「东西好不好」没有必然联系。

ev_data.calm: 「实验室不会造假」是信任，不是检验。数据的价值取决于来源和方法——谁做的、样本多大、怎么测的。

ev_regret.calm: 最难的一个：反问（「你确定不买真的会后悔吗？」）听起来像提问，其实已经预设了「会后悔」。真正的检验，是把断言当成断言，问它有没有依据。

hints: 小心「反问」——它看起来像问题，其实已经替你下了结论
正确项不一定是问句：把断言当作断言去检验，也是批判性思维
「权威」「检测」「数据」这些词本身不是证据，来源和方法才是
zh.explanation: 这一关的六个冲动，每个都有「看似合理实则站不住」的选项：诉诸大众、权威符号、二元站队、小样本、信任代替检验——还有最难的反问式伪问题。批判性思维不是「会提问」，而是「能辨别真问题与假问题、会检验断言与证据」。

en.scenario: In the livestream, the host raises the "Season 3 new product": everyone is buying it! The authoritative lab report is right here! The barrage floods with "you'll regret not buying it"...

impulsePrompts.ev_conformity: Everyone is buying it, so it must be good!
impulsePrompts.ev_report: He's showing an "authoritative test report" — it must be fine!
impulsePrompts.ev_bw2: Either trust the host, or you're a hater — no middle ground!
impulsePrompts.ev_ego2: My friends all love it, so it must be fine!
impulsePrompts.ev_data: He showed lab data — there's nothing left to argue!
impulsePrompts.ev_regret: The barrage says "you'll regret not buying it"!

options.opt_snow: A million sold — the crowd is always right
options.opt_ask_c1: High sales prove good marketing — do they prove good quality?
options.opt_rhet: Everyone is buying, are you the only smart one?
options.opt_seal: The report is stamped, what else is there to doubt?
options.opt_ask_c5: Who issued the test report? What exactly was tested?
options.opt_doubt: A stamped report is obviously real, don't overthink
options.opt_accept: I just don't trust this host, so I'm a hater — so what?
options.opt_ask_c3: Does questioning the host mean rejecting everything he says?
options.opt_echo: The haters have a point too
options.opt_friends: Friends wouldn't hurt me — their experience is the realest data
options.opt_ask_c4: Can three friends' experiences represent all users?
options.opt_band: All my friends bought it — I'll look left out if I don't
options.opt_stubborn: The data is right there — questioning it is just trolling
options.opt_ask_c6: Which lab ran this data? How big was the sample?
options.opt_trust: The data must be real — labs don't fake results
options.opt_rhet2: Are you sure you won't really regret not buying it?
options.opt_check: "You'll regret it" — is there any evidence behind that claim?
options.opt_ignore: Whether I regret it is my own business, forget it

ev_conformity.calm: "The crowd is always right" and "are you the only smart one?" both pressure you with numbers, not evidence — sales are the result of marketing, not proof of quality.

ev_report.calm: A "stamp" is a symbol of authority, not evidence. Ask who issued the report, what was tested, and under what standard — symbols don't replace content.

ev_bw2.calm: "Questioning = hating" is binary rhetoric that forces you to pick a side. Real questioning is specific and reasoned — nothing like the "hater" label.

ev_ego2.calm: Friends' experiences are a tiny sample, and herd pressure is conformity too — "everyone bought it" has no necessary link to "it's good".

ev_data.calm: "Labs don't fake results" is trust, not scrutiny. A data set's value depends on its source and method — who ran it, sample size, how it was measured.

ev_regret.calm: The hardest one: a rhetorical question ("are you sure you won't regret it?") sounds like a question but already assumes "you will regret it". Real scrutiny treats the claim as a claim and asks for evidence.

hints: Beware rhetorical questions — they look like questions but already decide the answer for you
The right move is not always a question: testing a claim as a claim is critical thinking too
"Authority", "testing", "data" are not evidence in themselves — source and method are
en.explanation: All six impulses in this level hide plausible-but-unfounded options: appeal to the crowd, authority symbols, binary side-picking, small samples, trust instead of scrutiny — and the hardest, the rhetorical pseudo-question. Critical thinking is not "asking questions" — it is telling real questions from fake ones, and putting claims and evidence to the test.
